topline.text: Sheffield's exclusion rate rose 32% in 2024-25 — averaging six pupils a week, with secondary exclusions now second-worst among the core cities — a report to the council's finance and performance policy committee shows.
topline.action: Committee considers the report on Tuesday 22 September; worth watching what action it commits to.

topline.text: DfE has opened a £22.5m Enrichment Expansion Programme for 400+ disadvantaged mainstream, special and alternative provision secondary schools, funding music, sport, debating and outdoor learning clubs.
topline.action: Worth checking whether any MAPs schools are among the named beneficiaries.

diary.text: Sheffield's finance and performance policy committee considers the exclusions report — first test of what action follows the 32% rise.
NEU's national executive meets to decide whether to stand down the strike ballot, after DfE confirmed this year's pay rise is fully funded.

items.lede: Sheffield exclusions up 32% in a year — now second-worst among core cities.
items.body: A report going to Tuesday's finance and performance policy committee found secondary exclusions averaged six a week in 2024-25, with over a third linked to a single serious incident rather than persistent disruption. A small number of schools account for a disproportionate share, and the Sheffield Inclusion Centre — statutory alternative provision from day six — is nearing capacity. Cllr Douglas Johnson called the rise 'really alarming'. Figures are as reported ahead of the committee meeting; worth checking against the published papers once available.
items.action: Useful context if you're fielding questions about Inclusion Centre capacity or managed-move pressure this term.

items.lede: £22.5m enrichment drive targets 400+ disadvantaged secondary schools.
items.body: The Enrichment Expansion Programme funds music, sport, debating, engineering clubs and outdoor learning in mainstream, special and AP schools serving disadvantaged communities, building on the DfE's Enrichment Framework published in June. From this term, Ofsted assesses enrichment provision under personal development and wellbeing.
items.action: A lever worth flagging to schools still building out their enrichment offer.

box.text: Rise in Sheffield pupils excluded from school in 2024-25 — averaging six children a week — ahead of Tuesday's council committee report.
